 16.     RELIABILITY BACKSTOP

16.1.   Purpose

The Reliability Backstop provides a mechanism to resolve reliability criteria violations caused
by: (a) lack of sufficient capacity committed through the Reliability Pricing Model Auctions; or
(b) near-term transmission deliverability violations identified after the Base Residual Auction is
conducted. These backstop mechanisms are intended to guarantee that sufficient generation,
transmission and demand response solutions will be available to preserve system reliability. The
backstop mechanisms are based on specific triggers that signal a need for a targeted solution to a
reliability problem that was not resolved by the long-term commitment of Capacity Resources
through Self-Supply or the Reliability Pricing Model Auctions.

16.2    Investigation of Capacity Shortfall

Beginning with the 2032/2033 Delivery Year and thereafter, if the total Unforced Capacity of
Capacity Resources committed for a Delivery Year following the Base Residual Auction equates
to an installed reserve margin that is more than one percentage point lower than the approved
PJM Region Installed Reserve Margin, the Office of the Interconnection shall investigate the
cause for the shortage, and recommend corrective action, including, without limitation, adjusting
the Cost of New Entry to the extent determined necessary by such investigation, or addressing
other barriers to entry identified by such investigation. No Reliability Backstop Auction will be
conducted to address such a shortfall unless it occurs in the Base Residual Auctions for three
consecutive Delivery Years beginning with the 2032/2033 Delivery Year and thereafter.

16.3    Triggering Conditions

       a)      Either of the following two conditions will trigger reliability backstop measures
provided in this section, as described below:

               i)      If the total Unforced Capacity of all Capacity Resources committed
through Self-Supply or the Base Residual Auctions for three consecutive Delivery Years
beginning with the 2032/2033 Delivery Year and thereafter, equates to an installed reserve
margin that is more than one percentage point lower than the approved PJM Region Installed
Reserve Margin, the Office of the Interconnection will declare a capacity shortage and make a
filing with FERC for approval to conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction. Upon receipt of such
approval, the Office of the Interconnection will conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction in
accordance with ection 16.4 below.

                ii)    If the total Unforced Capacity of all Base Load Generation Resources
committed in a Base Residual Auction for a Delivery Year is less than the forecasted minimum
hourly load calculated by the Office of the Interconnection for such Delivery Year, the Office of
the Interconnection will investigate the cause of shortfall. If such a shortfall occurs in the Base
Residual Auctions for three consecutive Delivery Years beginning with the 2032/2033 Delivery
Year and thereafter, the Office of the Interconnection shall declare a capacity shortage and make
a filing with FERC for approval to conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction. Upon receipt of such
 approval, the Office of the Interconnection will conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction in
accordance with section 16.4 below.

        b)       In addition to the foregoing events that trigger reliability backstop measures, if a
near-term, i.e., later in time than the conduct of the Base Residual Auction for a Delivery Year,
transmission criteria violation caused by an announced generation resource deactivation is
identified by the regional transmission reliability planning analysis performed by the Office of
the Interconnection in accordance with Part V of this Tariff, the Office of the Interconnection
will identify the necessary transmission upgrade. In accordance with such rules, such generation
resource may remain in service until the transmission upgrade is installed. No Reliability
Backstop Auction will be conducted.

16.4.   Reliability Backstop Auction

        a)     Scope of Auction

The Office of the Interconnection shall conduct each Reliability Backstop Auction to commit
additional Generation Capacity Resources, or in the case of an auction triggered by section
16.3(a)(ii), additional Base Load Generation Resources to the PJM Region to resolve the system-
wide reliability criteria violation that triggered the need for such auction. Capacity Resources
committed in a Reliability Backstop Auction for a Delivery Year shall not include any Planned
Generation Capacity Resources previously committed in the Base Residual Auction for such
Delivery Year. The Reliability Backstop Auction shall obtain commitments of additional
Generation Capacity Resources (or, as applicable, additional Base Load Generation Resources)
for a term of up to fifteen (15) Delivery Years. If a Reliability Backstop Auction is required, the
offer period for such auction shall commence, subject to FERC approval as specified above, no
later than four months after the Base Residual Auction in which the third consecutive Capacity
Resource shortfall occurs. Upon verification and notification by the PJM Board of Managers that
a Reliability Backstop Auction is required, the Office of the Interconnection shall post
notification that a Reliability Backstop Auction is to be held. Upon such notification, the offer
period shall commence, and shall remain open for six (6) months. PJMSettlement shall be the
Counterparty to the capacity transaction resulting from committed Capacity Resources clearing
the Reliability Backstop Auction.

        b)     Sell Offers

Each Sell Offer shall specify the following information, as further specified in the PJM Manuals:

        •      the minimum price in $/MW-day required by the Capacity Market Seller to
               provide additional Unforced Capacity from a Generation Capacity Resource (or
               from a Base Load Generation Resource, in the case of an auction triggered by
               section 16.3(a)(ii)) above;

        •      the megawatts of Unforced Capacity to be provided by such resource;

        •      the specific location of the proposed plant;
        •       all information required from a Generation Interconnection Customer by Tariff,
               Part IV and the PJM Manuals;

       •       general plant technical specifications, as specified in the PJM Manuals;

       •       the term of cost recovery (“Backstop Period”) requested, not to exceed 15 years;
               and

       •       the first full Delivery Year for which such resource shall be available, which shall
               also be the first year of the Backstop Period.

Each Generation Capacity Resource (or Base Load Generation Resource) accepted in a
Reliability Backstop Auction shall comply with the procedures for new generation
interconnection in Tariff, Part IV, and each such resource shall be responsible for satisfying all
capability and deliverability requirements for Capacity Resources, pursuant to the Reliability
Assurance Agreement.

       c)      Submission of Sell Offers

The Sell Offer period shall begin at 00:01 Eastern Prevailing Time on the date specified by the
Office of the Interconnection in the notification posting and shall end at 23:59 Eastern Prevailing
Time six calendar months after such date. Sell offers shall be submitted during such period in
writing to the Office of the Interconnection, and shall conform to the submission procedures as
specified in the PJM Manuals. The Office of the Interconnection shall confirm in writing the
receipt of each Sell Offer, within two weeks after receipt of each such offer.

       d)      Posting of Information by the Office of the Interconnection

Upon notification by the PJM Board of Managers that a Reliability Backstop Auction will be
conducted, the Office of the Interconnection shall post the following information:

       •       System condition that necessitates a Reliability Backstop Auction;

       •       Megawatt quantity of Unforced Capacity required from additional Generation
               Capacity Resources, or from additional Base Load Generation Resources;

       •       Date by which the resources must be capable of delivering Unforced Capacity;

       •       Any other required specifications for the additional Unforced Capacity sought
               through such auction.

       e)      Conduct of the Reliability Backstop Auction

               i)      Auction Clearing Procedure
 The Reliability Backstop Auction shall select the Sell Offer or combination of Sell Offers that
that satisfies the requirements posted by the Office of the Interconnection at the lowest offer
price(s). If more than one Sell Offer must be selected to satisfy the specified requirements, the
Sell Offers shall be selected in rank order from lowest offer price to highest offer price until the
requirement is satisfied. In the event two or more Sell Offers specify the same offer price, and
fewer than all of such offers are needed to satisfy the specified requirements, the Office of the
Interconnection shall select the Sell Offer(s) proposing Generation Capacity Resource(s), or, as
applicable, Base Load Generation Resource(s) that will best satisfy overall reliability
requirements for the PJM Region, as determined by the Office of the Interconnection using
transmission reliability analysis.

               ii)     Market Settlement

Pursuant to the agreement specified below, each Capacity Market Seller submitting a Sell Offer
that is accepted in a Reliability Backstop Auction shall be paid by PJMSettlement the offer price
in such Sell Offer for each MW-day in the Backstop Period, less any payments the Capacity
Market Seller is entitled to receive pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5 as a result of
Sell Offers submitted with respect to such Generation Capacity Resource in any Base Residual
Auction or Incremental Auction, including, without limitation, payments of Capacity Resource
Clearing Prices (including for Self-Supply) and Resource Make-Whole Payments; and less any
payments the Capacity Market Seller is entitled to receive for energy or ancillary services
pursuant to Operating Agreement, Schedule 1 with respect to services provided by such resource,
net of the Variable Operations and Maintenance costs of such resource, as determined in
accordance with the PJM Manuals.

PJM shall recover the costs of any such payments to Capacity Market Sellers for such resources
through a charge, in addition to the Locational Reliability Charge, assessed on all LSEs in the
PJM Region, pro rata based on each such LSE’s Daily Unforced Capacity Obligations in all
LDAs in which such LSE serves load. PJMSettlement shall be the Counterparty to the LSE’s
obligation to pay, and payment of, such charges.

               iii)    Standard Contract Provisions

PJMSettlement, will enter into an agreement with each Capacity Market Seller that submitted an
accepted Sell Offer in any Reliability Backstop Auction providing for the payments specified
above. Such agreement shall include the provisions and address the standards set forth in section
16.4(b) above, and shall include such other terms and conditions as are customary in the
industry, as specified in the PJM Manuals.

       f)      FERC Approval

Any such agreement shall provide that it shall be filed with FERC as a rate schedule pursuant to
section 205 of the Federal Power Act, and that the effectiveness of such agreement shall be
conditioned on receipt of FERC acceptance or approval of such agreement.

16.5   Must Offer into Base Residual Auction
 All Capacity Market Sellers submitting a Sell Offer that is selected in a Reliability Backstop
Auction must offer all Unforced Capacity of the Generation Capacity Resource underlying such
Sell Offer into the Base Residual Auctions conducted subsequent to the Reliability Backstop
Auction for all Delivery Years in the Backstop Period. The Market Seller shall offer the
Unforced Capacity of such resources into each such auction at zero price, and shall receive the
Capacity Resource Clearing Price as determined in each such auction.

16.6   Reliability Backstop Resource Deficiency Charges

       (a)     Any Capacity Market Seller that submits a Sell Offer that was selected in a
Reliability Backstop Auction and that is not able to deliver in a Delivery Year all megawatts of
Unforced Capacity specified in the selected Sell Offer, shall not receive any payments that such
Capacity Market Seller otherwise would have been eligible to receive for such Delivery Year
pursuant to the Reliability Backstop Auction.

        (b)     Any Capacity Market Seller that submits a Sell Offer that was selected in a
Reliability Backstop Auction and that fails to deliver all megawatts of Unforced Capacity
specified in the selected Sell Offer at any time during the Backstop Period specified in such Sell
Offer must refund all payments received by such Market Seller pursuant to section 16.4(b)
above.
 18.    RELIABILITY BACKSTOP PROCUREMENT

The Reliability Backstop Procurement or “RBP” is a one-time procurement, starting in 2026, to
address resource adequacy challenges in the PJM Region arising from insufficient capacity
committed through Reliability Pricing Model Auctions starting in the 2027/2028 Delivery Year.
 18.1   Determination of Final RBP Target

The Reliability Backstop Procurement is designed to procure sufficient RBP UCAP MW to meet
the Final RBP Target.

        (a)    Initial RBP Target
The Initial RBP Target shall be a region-wide value equal to the UCAP MW quantity PJM clears
short of the PJM Region Reliability Requirement for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year Base Residual
Auction.

        (b)   Final RBP Target
The Final RBP Target shall be a PJM region-wide value equal to the Initial RBP Target minus the
total PJM region-wide Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW and the unforced capacity obligation
value of load that have successfully requested and obtained an opt-out pursuant to Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.1(d).

        (c)    Fixed Resource Requirement Entities
Fixed Resource Requirement (“FRR”) Entities as of the 2028/2029 Delivery Year shall be
excluded from the Reliability Backstop Procurement, including Initial and Final RBP Targets.
To the extent an Electric Distributor zone/area that has RBP UCAP MW committed through the
Reliability Backstop Procurement later becomes an FRR Service Area pursuant to RAA, Schedule
8.1.D, the Electric Distributor zone/area shall continue to be accountable for the RBP UCAP MW
quantity committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement.

        (d)     Opt-Out
When calculating the Final RBP Target, the Initial RBP Target shall also be decremented where
the Electric Distributor’s zone/area has rates that are not regulated by the states and is unable to
address cost allocation associated with capacity procured in the backstop. Such request by the
Electric Distributor shall specify the associated MW quantity of load in the zone/area that will be
opted-out of the Initial RBP Target and be accompanied by supporting documentation
demonstrating an inability to address cost allocation associated with capacity procured in the
backstop, along with written support for such opt-out from the relevant state governor, RERRA,
and interconnection customer(s). The Initial RBP Target shall be further decremented, if requested
by an Electric Distributor, by up to the associated MW quantity of load that participates in a peak
shaving adjustment program where such Electric Distributor’s zone/area addresses their capacity
needs through peak shaving adjustment programs that are codified in state law and that also meet
the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD-2.
 18.2   Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

         (a)     Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW is capacity that (i) has not previously supported
a capacity commitment or been committed in an FRR Plan as of the commencement of the
Reliability Backstop Procurement; and (ii) is supplied by a resource that satisfies each of the
criteria set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.2(b).

       (b)     Resources Eligible to Supply Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

A resource eligible to supply Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW must have an expected
commercial operation date, or is reasonably expected to be an Annual Demand Resource or DER
Capacity Aggregation Resource that will be registered with the Office of the Interconnection and
under a contract to perform based on PJM dispatch instructions, by no later than June 1, 2032 and
be: (i) a new build generation resource including new resources that obtain Capacity
Interconnection Rights transferred from deactivated resources or resources that have announced
deactivation as of April 10, 2026; (ii) the incremental capacity created by an uprate of existing
Generation Capacity Resources, but only to the extent such incremental capacity is created through
an increase in such Generation Capacity Resource’s installed capacity and increase in Capacity
Interconnection Rights associated with that Generation Capacity Resource; (iii) the incremental
capacity created by the utilization of Surplus Interconnection Service; (iv) repowering of a
deactivated generation resource that deactivated prior to April 10, 2026; (v) incremental capacity,
whether due to greater Unforced Capacity or a higher level of Capacity Interconnection Rights,
created by an existing Generation Capacity Resource’s changing fuel type to a more efficient fuel
type; or (vi) Planned Demand Resource or Planned DER Capacity Aggregation Resources, as
described in the RAA, Schedule 6 and Schedule 6.2.

       (c)     Evidence of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

During the RBP bid submission window defined in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.4, Electric
Distributors shall report the Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW in their respective zones/areas to
the Office of the Interconnection in accordance with their requirements set forth in the Operating
Agreement, section 11.3, and such report shall be accompanied by evidence of at least one of the
following supporting materials. Likewise, to the extent LSEs, interconnecting customers, large
loads, Transmission Owners, or other entities report Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW to the
Office of the Interconnection during such RBP bid submission window, the reported Qualifying
RBP Offset UCAP MW must be accompanied with evidence of at least one of the following
supporting materials:

              (i)    Signed bilateral contracts for Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW for at least
       five Delivery Years with a commercial operation date prior to the start of the 2032/2033
       Delivery Year, and matched with load that has an executed electric service agreement or
       transmission service agreement, indicating that the load will be coming online in the
       2027/2028 or 2028/2029 Delivery Year;

              (ii)  Self-Supply generation that is in a Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory
       Authority (“RERRA”)-approved or accepted integrated resource plan with either
        associated generation in the PJM interconnection queue or signed bilateral contracts for
       Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW for at least five Delivery Years with a commercial
       operation date prior to the start of the 2032/2033 Delivery Year, and matched with load
       that has an executed electric service agreement or transmission service agreement,
       indicating that the load will be coming online in the 2027/2028 or 2028/2029 Delivery
       Year; or

               (iii)  Signed commitment between a Curtailment Service Provider or DER
       Aggregator and new load(s) that has an executed electric service agreement or transmission
       service agreement, indicating that the new load(s) will, in a MW quantity equal to MW
       quantity of the new load(s), either (a) participate as Annual Demand Resources or DER
       Capacity Aggregation Resources starting in the 2028/2029 Delivery Year Second
       Incremental Auction and continuing through the 2032/2033 Delivery Year, or (b) purchase
       replacement Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW that are eligible generation or storage
       resources.

        (d)     To determine the quantity of any Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW that are
verified by the Office of the Interconnection and used to decrement the Initial RBP Target, the
Office of the Interconnection shall use the applicable ELCC Class Ratings from the Base Residual
Auction associated with the 2028/2029 Delivery Year, or the estimated unit-specific UCAP value
for resources with no ELCC Class Rating.

        (e)    The total quantity of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW verified by the Office of
the Interconnection and used to decrement the Initial RBP Target total amount allowed for each
zone/area will be capped at the Load Adjustment for each Electric Distributor zone/area amount
of summer 2028 demand as set forth in the load forecast.
 18.3    Cost Allocation of RBP Charges, Credits, and Shortfall Charges

       (a)     Cost Allocation to Electric Distributor zone/area

The Office of the Interconnection shall allocate the Initial RBP Target MW to each Electric
Distributor’s zone/area using that zone/area’s pro-rata share of the difference between the
forecasted Load Adjustments for the 2026/2027 Delivery Year and the 2028/2029 Delivery Year.

The difference between the forecasted Load Adjustments for the 2026/2027 and the 2028/2029
Delivery Years shall be reduced for the purpose of this calculation to the extent:

              (i)     an Electric Distributor, LSE, Transmission Owner, or other entity provides
       the Office of Interconnection with evidence of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW, in
       accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.2 and as may be further set forth in the
       PJM Manuals; or

               (ii)   an Electric Distributor zonee/area meets one of the opt-out provisions set
       forth in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.1(d).

The resulting reduced MW, floored at zero, is used to calculate the zone/area’s assigned pro-rata
share of the Final RBP Target MW. The zone/area’s assigned share of the Final RBP Target MW
shall remain constant throughout the fixed, 15-year term.

The Office of the Interconnection shall allocate the total RBP Charges, assessed daily, to an
Electric Distributor’s zone/area on a pro-rata basis using the zone/area’s assigned share of the total
Final RBP Target MW across all zone/areas.

       (b)     Cost Allocation to Load Serving Entities

              (i)     The daily assessed RBP Charges allocated to each Electric Distributor
       zone/area shall be further allocated to each applicable LSE within that zone/area with an
       RBP Obligation (“RBO”) based on the LSE’s pro-rata share of the total RBP Obligation
       MW for the zone/area.

               (ii)   The RBP Charge assessed daily to an LSE in a zone/area shall be the LSE’s
       daily reported RBO MW in the zone/area divided by the total RBO MW in the zone/area
       multiplied by total, daily RBP Charges allocated to the zone/area.

               (iii)  The RBO MW shall be, where available, the state and/or RERRA-
       determined allocation of cleared RBP UCAP MW to LSEs within each Electric
       Distributor’s zone/area, as reported by each Electric Distributor to the Office of the
       Interconnection, with the initial allocation reported no later than sixty (60) days prior to
       the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. If no RBO MW are reported to the Office of the
       Interconnection in an Electric Distributor zone/area, PJM will allocate the RBP Charges
       for that zone/area to all load in the zone/area using each LSE’s ratio share of the Daily
       Unforced Capacity Obligation for the zone/area as determined in RAA, Schedule 8.
 PJMSettlement shall be the Counterparty to each LSE’s obligation to pay, and payments
of, RBP Charges.

       (iv)    RBP Shortfall Charges will be allocated to LSEs as credits based on using
the same pro-rata share of the RBP Charges, pursuant to RAA, Section 7.2B.
 18.4   Scope of the Reliability Backstop Procurement

The Office of the Interconnection shall conduct an RBP to commit RBP Resources up to the UCAP
MW value to meet the Final RBP Target. The Reliability Backstop Procurement offer submission
window for RBP Sell Offers shall open for three weeks in 2026. The clearing and selection process
will take place thereafter and concluding six weeks following the close of the offer submission
window. The Office of the Interconnection shall notify RBP Sellers that receive a commitment as
an RBP Resource as soon as practicable upon the conclusion of the RBP. The Office of the
Interconnection shall post specific dates on the PJM website prior to the commencement of the
Reliability Backstop Procurement.

RBP Sellers may submit RBP Sell Offers of RBP Resources supporting RBP UCAP MW into the
Reliability Backstop Procurement. PJMSettlement shall be the Counterparty to the transactions
arising from the RBP.

An RBP Sell Offer will be considered binding once any PJM-identified deficiencies are cured and
until the conclusion of the Reliability Backstop Procurement and the underlying resource does not
receive a commitment in the Reliability Backstop Procurement.

The Reliability Backstop Procurement shall offer commitments for RBP UCAP MW for a fixed
period of fifteen (15) Delivery Years, starting with the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. Resources with
a commercial operation date later than the 2028/2029 Delivery Year shall be committed for the
remainder of the fifteen-year term of the Reliability Backstop Procurement commitment period,
i.e. through the end of the 2042/2043 Delivery Year.
 18.5   The Reliability Backstop Procurement Process

      (a)    RBP Seller Eligibility to Participate and General Requirements for Resources
Supporting RBP UCAP MW

To be eligible to participate in the Reliability Backstop Procurement, an RBP Seller must meet the
RBP credit requirements, set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8, with RBP Sell Offer(s)
for RBP UCAP MW based on a resource that:

               (i)     Has a commercial operation date, or is reasonably expected to be an Annual
       Demand Resource or DER Capacity Aggregation Resource that will be registered with the
       Office of the Interconnection and under a contract to perform based on PJM dispatch
       instructions, by no later than June 1, 2032, inclusive of any required Network Upgrades;

               (ii)  Has not received a capacity commitment or been committed in an FRR Plan
       as of the commencement of the Reliability Backstop Procurement;

               (iii)   Is not supplying Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW;

              (iv)   To the extent the subject of a notice of intent for the 2028/2029 Base
       Residual Auction, must have offered and not cleared in the 2028/2029 Base Residual
       Auction;

              (v)    To the extent the subject of a notice of intent for the 2029/2030 Base
       Residual Auction, must be offered into the 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction; and

               (vi)    Meets the requirements in Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 18.5(b), 18.5(c),
       or 18.5(d).

       (b)     Generation or Energy Storage Resources as an RBP Resource

To qualify as an RBP Resource, a generation or Energy Storage Resource that supplies RBP UCAP
MW eligible to be offered into the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall be in the PJM Region
or meet the requirements to pseudo-tie into the PJM Region in Tariff, Attachment DD, section
5.5A(b), must meet the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(a) and must be:

               (i)     Composed of new Installed Capacity and new Maximum Facility Output;

              (ii)    Supported by new Capacity Interconnection Rights (if located in the PJM
       Region) or Capacity Interconnection Rights transferred from a deactivated resource or a
       resource that announced deactivation as of April 10, 2026; and

              (iii)  Consist of (1) new build; (2) incremental capacity created by an uprate of
       an existing Generation Capacity Resource’s or Energy Storage Resource’s installed
       capacity and associated level of Capacity Interconnection Rights; or (3) repowering of a
        generation resource that had deactivated, or announced deactivation, on or before April 10,
       2026.

       (c)    RBP Demand Resources

To qualify as a Demand Resource that supplies RBP UCAP MW eligible to be offered into the
Reliability Backstop Procurement, a Demand Resource must meet the requirements of Tariff,
Attachment DD, sections 18.5(a), and:

               (i)    Not be reliant on or composed of registered location(s) that previously
       supported a Demand Resource that provided capacity in a prior Delivery Year unless such
       location represents an incremental increase in capacity resulting from an investment in new
       generation or new storage resources at that location; and

               (ii)    Identify, as part of its RBP Sell Offer, for the full length of the fixed term,
       the location(s) and associated participation contract(s).

       (d)    RBP DER Aggregation Resources

To qualify as a DER Capacity Aggregation Resource that supplies RBP UCAP MW eligible to be

Attachment C




       Affidavit of Ms. Danielle Croop,
Senior Manager in the Market Design group of
        PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.
                     UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                           BEFORE THE
             FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                           )
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                )               Docket No. ER26-____-000
                                           )

                   AFFIDAVIT OF DANIELLE CROOP
              ON BEHALF OF PJM INTERCONNECTION, L.L.C.

1.    My name is Danielle Croop, Senior Manager in the Market Design group for PJM
      Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”). My business address is 2750 Monroe Blvd.,
      Audubon, Pennsylvania, 19403. I am submitting this affidavit on behalf of PJM to
      support the proposed reforms to PJM’s Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”)
      and PJM’s Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load Serving Entities
      (“RAA”) to implement the Reliability Backstop Procurement (“RBP”) framework
      by providing support for PJM’s proposal to:
         a. Establish a region-wide procurement target for the RBP;
         b. Require that supply meet certain criteria to be eligible to reduce the Initial
            RBP Target, which differs from the criteria for supply eligible to be RBP
            Resources;
         c. Require that supply meet certain criteria to be eligible to submit RBP Sell
            Offers as RBP Resources, which differs from the criteria for supply eligible
            to reduce the Initial RBP Target;
         d. Rely on a pay-as-bid clearing structure based on a MW-weighted average
            of the levelized procurement cost cap equal to $555/megawatt (“MW”)-day
            Unforced Capacity (“UCAP”);
         e. Select resources based on a MW-weighted average of the levelized
            procurement cost;
         f. Not propose explicit market power screening or mitigation measures as part
            of the RBP;
         g. Settle RBP Resource commitments based on contract for difference
            (“CfD”) Structure; and
         h. Proposed Cost Allocation Methodology.

      In addition, I am sponsoring one exhibit, appended to my affidavit as Exhibit 1 and
      entitled RBP Selection Process Examples. Exhibit 1 contains three simplified
      examples that help demonstrate how the RBP selection process works.

QUALIFICATIONS

2.    In my role as Senior Manager for PJM, I lead a team of Market Design Specialists
      and Economists on the development of PJM’s market design across all of PJM’s
      markets including the energy, ancillary services, and capacity markets. My
      responsibilities include leading the development of wholesale market rules and
          participation frameworks that advance market efficiency and grid reliability. I
         joined PJM in 2014 as an Engineer, and since then, I have held numerous other
         roles, including as a Senior Engineer, Senior Lead Engineer, Senior Lead Market
         Design Specialist, and Market Design Manager, providing technical support and
         leading cross-divisional teams on market design, market evolution initiatives
         related to energy storage and distributed energy technologies participating in the
         PJM markets, and balancing operations at PJM, including involvement in a number
         of North American Electric Reliability Corporation subcommittees and initiatives.

3.       Prior to joining PJM, I was employed by the SI Organization, Inc. as a System
         Engineer supporting large system integrations. I received a Bachelor of
         Engineering Degree and a Master of Engineering (Electrical Engineering) from
         Drexel University in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and have obtained a Certificate in
         Engineering Management.

I.       KEY DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS AND RATIONALE

4.       PJM is aiming to commence a procurement of new capacity resources through the
         RBP1 on September 30, 2026. PJM will set a procurement target for the RBP,
         calculated as the shortfall MW from the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction
         (“BRA”), as adjusted to reflect voluntarily contracted new capacity procured by
         load coming on the PJM system in the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 Delivery Years
         and any supported load that opts-out of the procurement. The shortfall MW from
         the 2028/2029 BRA was 6,831.3 MW of UCAP below the Regional Transmission
         Organization (“RTO”) Reliability Requirement.

5.       The RBP will function as a safety net to address the shortfall MW from the
         2028/2029 BRA that has not been addressed by new load bringing their own new
         capacity through bilateral agreements or otherwise. The RBP is a stop-gap, one-
         time measure aimed specifically at addressing the resource adequacy shortfall in
         the PJM Region, an effort design to work in part with the load that has voluntarily
         brought supply to the PJM Region—independently or with support of ongoing PJM
         bilateral matching efforts—and a return to market fundamentals to support the
         expected load growth over the next decade. The RBP seeks to obtain “RBP
         Resources,” a new, defined term in the Tariff, for a fixed, 15-year period, which
         will be set from the 2028/2029 Delivery Year to the 2042/2043 Delivery Year. The
         commitment term of the RBP Resources will vary by each resource’s commercial
         operation date. Those RBP Resources with a commercial operation date later than
         2028/2029 will have a shorter commitment, and the RBP commitments will not
         extend beyond the 2042/2043 Delivery Year.

6.       PJM will run the procurement mechanism as a pay-as-bid, capacity-only structure,
         with a MW-weighted average levelized procurement cost maximum willingness to
         pay equal to $555/MW-day UCAP across all Delivery Years. PJM will commit

1
 All capitalized terms that are not otherwise defined herein have the meaning defined in the Tariff, Amended
and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., or the RAA.


                                                     2
        resources at an RTO-level. The total costs of the daily RBP Charges will be
       allocated to Load Serving Entities (“LSE”) within a zone/area that had forecasted
       load growth, based on an RBP Obligation (“RBO”) MW, which is a newly defined
       term that incorporates state-determined allocations of RBP UCAP MW to LSEs
       and end-use customers, where available, that I elaborate on further, below.

II.    REGION-WIDE PROCUREMENT OF RBP RESOURCES

7.     The RBP is being driven by the resource adequacy shortfall at the RTO level.
       Therefore, the RBP aims to pool the supply and demand at the RTO level to address
       this shortfall. PJM does not propose to match specific supply to specific demand
       or to apply locational constraints in the central procurement.

8.     PJM recognizes there are locational considerations at large for resource adequacy,
       and these constraints are modeled in the Reliability Pricing Model (“RPM”). RPM
       is an annual three-year forward framework, which allows PJM to model the
       necessary locational parameters—Capacity Emergency Transfer Objectives
       (“CETO”) and Capacity Emergency Transfer Limits (“CETL”)—to accurately
       capture the locational needs in the capacity market. By contrast, PJM does not
       project and calculate these parameters 15-years out, which is the eligible term of
       the RBP, because PJM does not have the information needed to determine such
       locational parameters for 15-year term capacity commitments.

9.     PJM’s interconnection process ensures the initial deliverability of new capacity to
       the RTO. Going forward, the PJM Regional Transmission Expansion Plan
       (“RTEP”) process annually studies and addresses any transmission upgrades
       needed to ensure the ongoing deliverability of capacity resources. Load
       deliverability is also assessed as part of the RTEP process, which will identify
       transmission needs as load patterns change.

III.   INTENTIONALLY DIFFERENT REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPLY
       ELIGIBLE TO REDUCE THE INITIAL RBP TARGET AND SUPPLY
       ELIGIBLE TO SUBMIT RBP SELL OFFERS AS RBP RESOURCES

10.    PJM is proposing to reduce the Initial RBP Target MW by Qualifying RBP Offset
       UCAP MW, which is a new, defined term that represents net new capacity that
       meets certain qualifications. Importantly, the requirements to be Qualifying RBP
       Offset UCAP MW that may decrement the Initial RBP Target MW are different,
       and more inclusive than the requirements to qualify as RBP Resources with RBP
       UCAP MW that may submit sell offers in the RBP.

11.    The capacity provided by Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW and by RBP
       Resources that may sell RBP UCAP MW in the RBP have different obligations and
       therefore, PJM is proposing different criteria for these two categories of capacity.




                                            3
         A.       Supply Eligible to Reduce Initial RBP Target

12.     For supply to qualify as Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW, counterparties would
        be required to demonstrate the existence of commercial bilateral agreements or self-
        supply and show that the associated resources result in net new UCAP being made
        available to the PJM system. The following is a list of resources that could
        demonstrate net- new UCAP and would be considered in this case:

             a. New build including new resources that obtain Capacity Interconnection
                Rights (“CIR”) transferred from deactivated resources or resources that
                have announced deactivation as of April 10, 2026;

             b. Uprates (incremental Installed Capacity (“ICAP”)/CIR only);

             c. Repowering of deactivated generators that have retired as of April 10, 2026;

             d. Surplus interconnection (incremental only);

             e. Resources that undergo fuel-switching to another more efficient fuel type
                that results in a higher UCAP and CIR uprate (incremental only); and

             f. New Load Management (Emergency or Pre-emergency Demand Resources
                and Distributed Energy Resource (“DER”)) Capacity Aggregation
                Resources.

13.     PJM is defining this criterion broadly to capture all meaningful sources of new
        UCAP serving new load that contribute to resource adequacy and prevent double
        procuring for new load that is bringing new capacity to the system.

        B.       Supply Eligible to Participate as RBP Resources in the RBP

14.     Resources eligible to participate as RBP Resources in the RBP, if accepted, will be
        procured up through the end of a fixed, 15-year capacity commitment. PJM
        believes additional requirements are necessary to ensure that resources permitted
        to participate in the RBP align with the underlying objectives of the procurement
        to obtain new physical capacity for the system and demonstrate a high likelihood
        of successfully entering service and remaining available throughout the
        commitment period.

15.     The RBP Resource eligibility criteria are comparatively more restrictive than the
        criteria for Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW, and specifically in addition to
        requiring new UCAP be brought to the system, there is a requirement that there is
        new ICAP and Maximum Facility Output (“MFO”) being brought to the system,
        and new or transferred CIRs.2 These additional requirements remove the eligibility
        of two defined sources of new UCAP that may be Qualifying New UCAP MW and

2
 CIRs can be transferred from a deactivated resource or a resource that has announced deactivation as of
April 10, 2026.


                                                   4
       eligible to reduce the Initial RBP Target. More specifically, the following are not
      eligible to serve as RBP Resources:

         a. Surplus interconnection (incremental only); and

         b. Resources that undergo fuel-switching to another more efficient fuel type
            that results in a higher UCAP or CIR uprate (incremental only).

16.   These more restrictive eligibility requirements are intended to ensure that resources
      receiving long-term commitments are capable of delivering the reliability benefits
      that the RBP is designed to secure, reduce risk, and improve confidence in project
      execution.

17.   The exclusion of Surplus Interconnection Service (“SIS”) resources from supply
      eligible to serve as RBP Resources was driven by the fact that these projects do not
      bring any additional MFO or CIRs to the system. This is a defined requirement for
      resources entering through the SIS-defined Tariff provisions. Resources that do
      interconnect and operate under SIS do not have any rights on their own to the PJM
      system. By design, a surplus resource can only operate while the existing resource
      is in service, or no more than one year after the deactivation of the existing resource,
      and when the existing resource is not operating and using the interconnection
      service. Given the 15-year term, resources need to be able to operate independently
      to provide certainty of deliverability for a 15-year term. Further, these projects,
      while increasing UCAP in a hybrid configuration, do not have clear contributions
      of UCAP between the existing resource and surplus resource creating uncertainty
      and the need for sensitivities or estimates in both the increase system capacity and
      the RBP settlements.

18.   This is not a complete barrier to participation of surplus resources in RBP. As
      mentioned above, these resources are able to participate as Qualifying New UCAP
      MW to reduce the Initial RBP Target. Further, these sited projects would still have
      an opportunity to offer into the RBP and co-locate with the existing resource and
      be studied by PJM for increased CIRs and MFO at the facility through the
      interconnection process.

19.   The exclusion of resources that undergo fuel-switching to another more efficient
      fuel type that results in a higher UCAP and CIR uprate (incremental only) is also
      necessary to provide the certainty of deliverability for a 15-year term expected from
      an RBP Resource. Fuel switching does not bring new ICAP or new MFO on to the
      system. There is an anticipated UCAP increase resulting in the resource Effective
      Load Carrying Capability (“ELCC”) class change and resulting accreditation,
      however the potential new UCAP captured from this resource would require some
      estimate of the incremental UCAP value, which may require sensitivity analyses,
      to determine the delivered incremental UCAP and RBP payment, that cannot be
      based on any direct increase in ICAP for the resource. This creates uncertainty in
      what capacity will be available to the system in the 15-year term and should be
      settled under the RBP.


                                             5
 20.   Additionally, PJM has proposed more stringent requirements on Demand
      Resources and DER Aggregation Resources eligible to qualify as RBP Resources
      relative to the requirements on such resources for purposes Qualifying RBP Offset
      UCAP MW. Specifically, to qualify as RBP Resources, Demand Resources and
      DER Aggregation Resources need to have contracts for the RBP term (i.e., up to
      15 years) with the identified sites that are offering as RBP Resources. This is to
      provide assurance that the supply will be available for the 15-year term and manage
      the risk of the supply being available for the full term that PJM is procuring on
      behalf of load in the RBP. By contrast, Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW does
      not require 15-year contracts because the commitment terms (length, price, etc.) are
      being managed by the commercial contract between the buyer and seller.

IV.   PAY-AS-BID STRUCTURE

21.   PJM generally supports a single-clearing-price market design and continues to view
      uniform clearing prices as the most efficient market outcome. Uniform pricing
      promotes transparent price discovery, facilitates forward pricing, and supports
      competitive market outcomes and the PJM Region sees the benefits of that design
      across its existing markets.

22.   However, the proposed RBP differs significantly from PJM’s standard market
      constructs and warrants a different settlement approach which is why PJM is
      proposing a pay-as-bid structure for several reasons unique to this procurement.

23.   First, the RBP is intended as a one-time procurement mechanism designed to
      address near-term resource adequacy challenges while PJM continues to focus on
      long-term market fundamentals and supporting continued commercial bilateral
      contracting. Because this procurement is not designed to be a durable or repeatable
      procurement, its pricing outcomes are less likely to serve as incentive market
      signals.

24.   Second, much of the longer-term capacity that the RBP framework seeks to secure
      is expected to be obtained through bilateral arrangements outside of PJM’s
      organized markets. A pay-as-bid structure more closely aligns with the economics
      and settlement structures of bilateral contracts and reduces the likelihood that RBP
      outcomes will distort or influence those private contracting activities.

25.   Finally, the proposed procurement is not acquiring a uniform commodity.
      Although the RBP will seek a fixed, 15-year period of time for procurement and
      cost allocation of RBP Resources, those resources may differ based on contract
      duration (dependent on the projected in-service date of selected resources),
      commercial operation dates, and other factors such as differences in ELCC
      accreditation and varying UCAP across the full term of the commitment. These
      differences create distinct products rather than a single homogeneous offering.
      Establishing a uniform clearing price across such varied products would require
      PJM to normalize offers through potentially complex and subjective assumptions.




                                           6
       A pay-as-bid structure avoids those challenges while providing a straightforward
      and transparent procurement framework.

V.    VOLUME-WEIGHTED    LEVELIZED      COST    PROCUREMENT
      MAXIMUM WILLINGNESS TO PAY OF $555/MW-DAY UCAP

26.   PJM believes it is necessary to identify, for the RBP, a maximum willingness to
      pay because it is not reasonable to assume that load should be obligated to pay an
      unlimited amount for supply. As with other PJM procurement mechanisms, an
      upper bound helps balance reliability needs with customer cost protections.

27.   In this procurement, PJM is not receiving direct buy bids or an explicit expression
      of loads’ maximum willingness to pay, and thus PJM is proposing an administrative
      maximum willingness to pay that PJM believes will appropriately balance
      reliability needs and customer cost protections.

28.   The RPM relies on the Variable Resource Requirement (“VRR”) curve, which is
      derived from the Cost of New Entry, to establish the value PJM is willing to pay
      for resource commitments in a given Delivery Year. Specifically, for the
      2028/2029 Delivery Year BRA, absent the temporary price collar, Point 1 on the
      VRR curve is $555MW-day UCAP. Because the RBP is intended to address a
      specific resource shortfall identified in the 2028/2029 BRA, PJM is proposing to
      use Point 1 of the applicable BRA VRR curve as the basis for establishing the
      procurement maximum willingness to pay for the RBP.

29.   PJM is proposing an RBP maximum willingness to pay to be a MW-weighted
      average of the levelized procurement cost of all selected RBP Sell Offers to be set
      at $555/MW-day across all Delivery Years. This results in the cost to load being
      allocated for RBP Charges to not exceed $555/MW-day, on average, over the 15-
      year term. Using this average/budget approach to the maximum willingness to pay
      (in comparison to providing a price cap in each Delivery Year or a direct price cap
      on offers) allows more flexibility in supply sell offers, to the extent that a
      $555/MW-day maximum willingness to pay may not capture every resource’s costs
      and eliminates a potential barrier to supply participation.

VI.   SELECTION PROCESS

30.   PJM is proposing to calculate a levelized procurement cost for each RBP Sell Offer
      to determine the selection. The levelized cost of capacity is an industry standard
      evaluation metric used in competitive resource procurements across the country.
      The levelized cost calculation for evaluation addresses the fundamental issue of a
      simple MW-weighted average cost by accounting for the time value of money,
      which is critical when evaluating contracts spanning 15-year terms, as PJM is
      proposing in the RBP. Levelizing properly discounts future cost streams to a
      common basis, giving us a true economic comparison across bids. In Exhibit 1,
      appended to my affidavit, I provide examples, with step-by-step explanations,
      which illustrate how PJM’s proposed selection process will work.



                                           7
 31.    The calculation PJM will use is: Levelized Cost ($/MW-day) = Net Present Value
       (RBP Sell Offer price * UCAP offered)/Net Present Value (UCAP offered), with a
       discount rate equal to 9.5% after-tax average weighted average cost of capital
       (“ATWACC”). The proposed discount rate is The Brattle Group-estimate
       calculated value used in the 2025 Periodic Review of VRR Curve Shape and Key
       Parameters.3 The purpose of discounting is not to forecast inflation or market
       prices, but to reflect the time value of money and the opportunity cost of invested
       capital. The levelized cost is intended to represent the cost per UCAP unit needed
       to recover investment and operating costs over the offer term, and the ATWACC
       represents the economically appropriate discount rate. ATWACC represents the
       minimum expected return required by debt and equity holders and is therefore the
       standard rate used to annualize long-lived infrastructure costs.

VII.   MARKET MITIGATION

32.    PJM is not proposing market power screening or mitigation measures as part of the
       RBP. The RBP is designed as a pay-as-bid procurement in which each selected
       resource is compensated based on its individual offer rather than a market-clearing
       price established by the marginal resource. As a result, the traditional incentive and
       ability to exercise market power are substantially reduced.

33.    While the pay-as-bid design on its own does not eliminate market power concerns,
       the overall proposed RBP design further mitigates market power concerns. This is
       driven by the one-time nature of the procurement, the voluntary participation
       model, the limited scope and bilateral process, and the maximum willingness to
       pay. In a pay-as-bid approach, unlike a uniform clearing price construct where
       sellers are expected to offer a marginal cost, sellers are more likely to offer the
       expected clearing price. Given offers will likely have less variation and information
       underlying offers it can be difficult and ineffective to determine offers exhorting
       market power.

34.    The procurement is voluntary, meaning suppliers can simply choose to participate
       or not, and then further PJM is proposing a maximum willingness-to-pay cap,
       which provides a direct limit on procurement costs even in the absence of offer
       mitigation. The illustrative example below demonstrates the inability for one
       resource to impact the clearing price of any other resource in a pay-as-bid structure.




3
  2025 Periodic Review of Variable Resource Requirement Curve Shape and Key Parameters, PJM
Interconnection,                L.L.C.                  (Nov.                7,           2025),
https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercDockets/9248/20251107-er25-455-000.pdf
[https://perma.cc/87GP-AYL5].


                                               8
         This is in contrast to a uniform clearing price market where the marginal resource
        will set the clearing price and all resources will receive that price. A Seller has a
        fleet of three resources: A, B, and C and offers accordingly:

                Resource A @$10/MW-day

                Resource B @$10/MW-day

                Resource C @$50/MW-day

                Uniform-clearing price structure:

                     •   Resource C sets the market-clearing price at $50/MW-day,

                     •   Resource A and Resource B also receive the market-clearing price
                         of $50/MW-day

                Pay-as-bid structure:

                     •   Resource C receives offer price of $50/MW-day

                     •   Resource A receives offer price of $10/MW-day

                     •   Resource B receives offer price of $10/MW-day

VIII. CONTRACT FOR DIFFERENCE

37.     CfD is a financial settlement methodology for energy contracts designed to provide
        price stability to both the buyer (load) and seller (supply). It is structured around a
        “strike price” where the settlement or CfD is based on a difference between the
        market price and a committed strike price. If the strike price is higher than the
        market price, the buyer must pay the difference between the strike price and market

38.     PJM is proposing to settle the RBP with a CfD-like structure, where the strike price
        will be the RBP offer price of the committed RBP Resource for an applicable
        Delivery Year, and the market price will be the weighted average RPM clearing
        prices for the same applicable Delivery Year.
39.     PJM is proposing the CfD will only be assessed for MW that are committed in the
        RPM and delivered and will be capped at RBP committed MW. This is to say there
        will not be a CfD on RBP Resource committed MW that are not delivered in the
        applicable Delivery Year. This is a deviation from the purely financial CfD where
        the settlement would be on the committed amount, not what was physically
        delivered. PJM’s design choice of not designing a fully financial CfD was driven
        by the underscoring goal of the RBP supporting reliability and resource adequacy,
        and intended to preserve market participation while creating a more stable capacity
        revenue stream for the RBP Resource.

IX.     RBP COST ALLOCATION METHODOLOGY

40.     As a wholesale market operator, PJM’s role is to design and administer a
        procurement mechanism that addresses regional reliability needs in a manner
        consistent with our regulatory framework. Cost allocation decisions should
        therefore be grounded in principles that appropriately assign costs to beneficiaries
        (demand) while respecting the jurisdictional boundaries between wholesale market
        operations and retail rate design. This jurisdictional reality was also recognized in
        the Statement of Principles Regarding PJM signed by the National Energy
        Dominance Council and the 13 governors of the PJM states, issued on January 16,
        2026, where PJM’s 13 governors agreed to:

                [u]se their Authorities to Allocate Costs to Data Centers and Protect
                Residential Customers: Use all available authorities to ensure that
                their state public utility commissions design rate class structures to
                ensure that their states’ LSEs allocate their share of the cost to
                procure new capacity through the Reliability Backstop Auctions to
                new data center loads that have not otherwise procured capacity or
                agreed to be curtailable.5

41.     The cost allocation structure is designed around first allocating the Final RBP
        Target to Electric Distributor zones/areas with forecasted load adjustment, and then
        further allocating the charges to LSEs based on the RBO, which permits states to
        determine the appropriate allocation of RBP UCAP MW to specific LSEs and/or
        end-use customers, thus allowing Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authorities
        (“RERRA”) to appropriately assign costs to their respective retail customers,
        including data centers. Should the relevant RERRA(s) decline to communicate
